candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish ACE-inhibitor dry cough from angioedema and identify the cough as a recognized lisinopril class effect.

options.A: The cough indicates impending laryngeal angioedema and requires epinephrine despite the absence of swelling.
options.B: The cough shows the lisinopril dose is subtherapeutic and should be increased before the next blood-pressure check.
options.C: A persistent nonproductive cough is a recognized ACE-inhibitor class effect related to bradykinin accumulation.
options.D: The cough is unrelated to lisinopril because ACE-inhibitor respiratory adverse effects always include edema.

candidate.rationale: Persistent nonproductive cough is a recognized ACE-inhibitor class effect, attributed to reduced degradation of endogenous bradykinin. It is distinct from angioedema, which involves swelling and may threaten the airway. The cough does not indicate an inadequate dose, and its absence of swelling does not make a medication relationship unlikely.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A persistent nonproductive cough is a recognized ACE-inhibitor/lisinopril adverse effect and is clinically distinct from angioedema with swelling/airway symptoms.
